title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
description: Official 200-question Board Licensure Examination (Aug 18, 2019, Set B) covering Community Nutrition, Public Health Programs, Nutrition Assessment, and Philippine Nutrition Laws.

cards.front: The section in the program plan that defines the program vision, its significance, program scope, and projected outcome is called
cards.rationale: The program overview (or executive summary/project prospectus) sets the strategic stage for the entire program plan. It articulates the overarching vision, justifies why the initiative is significant (rationalization based on situational data), defines the operational scope (geographical boundaries, target beneficiaries, timeframe), and outlines the expected long-term outcomes and impacts.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Program overview gives the big-picture rationale before detailed operational methodologies and schedules are specified.

cards.front: What is the step in program planning where it involves identifying approaches necessary for the implementation of the program?
cards.rationale: Strategy formulation involves selecting the broad courses of action, methods, and intervention pathways (e.g., direct feeding, fortification, social behavioral change communication) necessary to achieve defined program goals and objectives.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Defining strategies bridges problem analysis/objective setting with detailed tactical activities.

cards.front: The continual monitoring - in a community, region or country - of factors or conditions that indicate, relate to or impinge on the nutritional status of individuals or groups of people is called
cards.rationale: According to the WHO and the National Nutrition Council (NNC), Nutrition Surveillance is the continuous and systematic collection, analysis, interpretation, and dissemination of nutritional and related socio-economic data to guide ongoing policy, program planning, and resource management.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Note the distinction between surveillance (continuous tracking for policy/action) and periodic surveys (one-time snapshots).

cards.front: It refers to the regular or periodic collection and evaluation of data that can be used to indicate present and future changes in nutritional status.
cards.rationale: In public health administration and NNC training manuals, systematic collection and evaluation of progress indicators to assess present trends and inform management decisions is termed evaluation and management (or monitoring/surveillance in broader epidemiological contexts). On the exam paper, option C is marked.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C (Evaluation and management). Notice the pairing of both collection and evaluation with managerial course-correction.

cards.front: Which of the following is an example of direct method of nutritional assessment?
cards.rationale: Nutritional assessment methods are divided into direct and indirect methods. Direct methods evaluate individual human subjects directly using the ABCD framework: Anthropometric, Biochemical/laboratory, Clinical, and Dietary methods. Vital health statistics, demographic data (age, sex), and agricultural/economic indicators are indirect ecological indicators.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Direct methods assess individual nutritional status directly; indirect methods evaluate community-level ecological proxies.

cards.front: What is the term used to define low weight for height?
cards.rationale: Under WHO Child Growth Standards adopted by the DOH and NNC: Low Weight-for-Height/Length (<-2 SD) defines Wasting (acute malnutrition/thinness); Low Height/Length-for-Age (<-2 SD) defines Stunting (chronic malnutrition); and Low Weight-for-Age (<-2 SD) defines Underweight (composite index).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Wasting = weight-for-height (acute deficit); Stunting = height-for-age (chronic deficit); Underweight = weight-for-age.

cards.front: What is the term used to define a situation in which food security is combined with a clean environment, adequate health services, and appropriate care and feeding practices, to ensure a healthy life for all household members?
cards.rationale: Nutrition Security extends beyond Food Security (which guarantees availability, accessibility, and affordability of food). Nutrition security integrates food security with sanitary environments, clean water, adequate primary healthcare, and optimal maternal and child caring/feeding practices to ensure physiological nutrient utilization for a healthy life.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Food security is necessary but not sufficient for nutrition security; sanitation, health, and care practices are the vital third pillar.

cards.front: As a RND, you are task to develop a program plan. What is the first step in developing your plan?
options: A. Plan for monitoring and evaluation
D. Set the goals and objectives
cards.rationale: The standard community nutrition program planning cycle always initiates with Situation Analysis / Community Assessment to identify and define the nutritional problems, their magnitude, distribution, and root causes before objectives can be formulated or interventions selected.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Order of program planning: 1) Identify/assess the problem -> 2) Set goals & objectives -> 3) Develop strategies/action plan -> 4) Implement -> 5) Monitor & Evaluate.

cards.front: The science and art of applying the principles of nutrition to the planning and preparation of foods, and management of the diet in relation to both health and disease is
cards.rationale: Under Republic Act No. 10862 (Nutrition and Dietetics Law of 2016) and classical professional definitions, Dietetics is the science and art of applying the principles of food and nutrition to the health and wellness of individuals and groups, disease prevention, and dietary management in illness.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Note: Item 161 in this same exam repeats this exact question stem, where option D was circled on the candidate's test paper.

cards.front: It refers to any activity, program or project that will contribute to change or improve the nutrition situation.
cards.rationale: A Nutrition Intervention is defined as any purposeful, planned activity, project, or policy designed to improve dietary intake, nutritional status, and health outcomes of an individual or target population.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Interventions encompass nutrition-specific direct actions (e.g. supplementation, feeding) and nutrition-sensitive structural actions.

cards.front: Which of the following is NOT a major program area of the Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition for the Year 2011 to 2016?
cards.rationale: Under the PPAN 2011–2016, the core strategic nutrition intervention programs focused on: 1) Infant and Young Child Feeding / Maternal and Child Health, 2) Micronutrient Supplementation, 3) Mandatory and Voluntary Food Fortification, 4) Supplementary Feeding, and 5) Nutrition in Emergencies. Human resource development is an institutional support / enabling mechanism rather than a primary intervention program area.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Distinguish between core nutritional intervention programs (MCH, supplementation, fortification) and general support/capacity building.

cards.front: The additional daily requirement of folate during pregnancy is
cards.rationale: According to the Philippine Dietary Reference Intakes (PDRI 2015), the Recommended Energy and Nutrient Intake (RENI) for folate for non-pregnant adult women is 400 mcg DFE/day. Pregnancy requires an additional +200 mcg DFE/day (total 600 mcg DFE/day) to support rapid fetal cell division, uterine enlargement, and prevent neural tube defects (NTDs).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Margin handwritten note: '200 ug. 150ug if lactating'. Non-pregnant RDA: 400 ug; Pregnant: +200 ug (total 600 ug); Lactating: +150 ug (total 550 ug).

cards.front: What is the indicator used to describe age-specific mortality rate, morbidity rates, or infant deaths?
cards.rationale: Mortality rates (such as infant mortality rate, neonatal mortality, under-five mortality) and morbidity rates broken down by age cohorts are vital demographic statistics and demographic health indicators used to assess population survival and disease burden.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D (Demographic). While closely tied to public health status, mortality/fertility/migration rates are fundamentally categorized as demographic indicators.

cards.front: Human milk has higher proportion of ________ a protein like lactalbumin which has a soft fluorescent curd in the infant's stomach.
cards.rationale: Human mature milk contains a whey-to-casein ratio of approximately 60:40 (and up to 80:20 in colostrum), compared to bovine milk which is 20:80. The predominant whey protein is alpha-lactalbumin, which forms a soft, flocculent (curd-like), easily digestible precipitate in the infant stomach.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C (whey). Human milk is predominantly whey (alpha-lactalbumin), forming soft flocculent curds; bovine milk is predominantly curd/casein.

cards.front: What is the process of integrating nutrition activities with other programs within the same sector?
cards.rationale: Intra-sectoral coordination/integration involves aligning and coordinating nutrition activities among different departments, divisions, or services within the same sectoral agency (e.g., integrating nutrition counseling within the Maternal, Neonatal, and Child Health program inside the Department of Health). Inter-sectoral involves distinct sectors (Health, Agriculture, Social Welfare, Education).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Intra = within the same sector (e.g. within DOH); Inter = between different sectors (e.g. DOH + DA + DSWD).

cards.front: What is the Executive Order that has regulated the marketing of breast milk substitutes or also known as Milk Code of the Philippines.
cards.rationale: Executive Order No. 51, signed on October 20, 1986 by President Corazon Aquino, is the 'National Code of Marketing of Breastmilk Substitutes, Breastmilk Supplements and Other Related Products', commonly known as the Philippine Milk Code. It regulates promotional activities, advertising, and donations of formula milk, feeding bottles, and teats.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. EO 51 = Philippine Milk Code (1986); RA 7600 = Rooming-In and Breastfeeding Act (1992); RA 10028 = Expanded Breastfeeding Promotion Act (2010).

cards.front: Which of the following agencies, as member of the NNC Board, that implements the basic needs program as a safety net provision of Republic Act 8435?
cards.rationale: Republic Act No. 8435 is the Agriculture and Fisheries Modernization Act of 1997 (AFMA). The Department of Agriculture (DA) is the lead implementing agency responsible for modernization, food security, and agricultural safety net provisions, and sits on the NNC Governing Board.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Margin handwritten note: 'promote industrialization agriculture, fisheries'. RA 8435 = AFMA under DA.

cards.front: Define what is evaluation?
cards.back: It measures the extent to which the objectives were met
options: A. It describes the community of interest
B. Collecting data to assess whether activities are implemented as planned
C. It is the process of resource generation
D. It measures the extent to which the objectives were met
cards.rationale: Evaluation is the systematic and objective assessment of an ongoing or completed project, program, or policy. Its purpose is to determine the relevance, fulfillment of objectives, developmental efficiency, effectiveness, impact, and sustainability. Option B describes monitoring.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Monitoring tracks whether activities are carried out as planned; Evaluation determines whether the planned objectives were actually achieved.

cards.front: What is the initial breast secretion produced by the post-partum woman?
cards.rationale: Colostrum is the yellowish, viscous pre-milk fluid produced by the mammary glands during late pregnancy and the first 2 to 4 days postpartum. It is uniquely high in secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA), lactoferrin, white blood cells, and epidermal growth factors, acting as the newborn's first natural immunization.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Colostrum is rich in antibodies (sIgA) and protein, lower in fat and lactose than mature breast milk.

cards.front: The PPAN has ________ projects serving as a framework for actions that could be undertaken by member agencies of the National Nutrition Council and other agencies.
cards.rationale: The Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition (PPAN 2017–2022) operational matrix encompasses 46 distinct projects structured across 12 strategic programs (8 nutrition-specific, 1 nutrition-sensitive, and 3 enabling support programs) executed by NNC member agencies and local government units.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Remember PPAN numbers: 12 Programs, 46 Projects. See also Item 143.

cards.front: The nutrient that aids in the absorption of calcium in any stage of life is
cards.rationale: Vitamin D, converted to its biologically active hormonal form 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 [calcitriol], stimulates the synthesis of calcium-binding proteins (calbindin-D9k) in the intestinal enterocytes, thereby facilitating active calcium and phosphorus absorption.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Calcitriol (active Vitamin D) is indispensable for intestinal calcium and phosphorus absorption.

cards.front: The current body status of a person or population groups related to their state of consumption and utilization of foods is ________
options: A. Weight for age z - score
cards.rationale: Nutritional Status is defined as the physiological condition of an individual or population resulting from the balance between nutrient intake, bioavailability, cellular utilization, and biological expenditure/losses.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. BMI and Z-scores are indices/metrics used to assess nutritional status, but the overarching physiological state is Nutritional Status.

cards.front: This pertains to the category of variables that can be measured using either the interval or ordinal scale of measurement.
cards.rationale: In research methodology and biostatistics, variables are classified into continuous/quantitative or categorical/qualitative scales. Ordinal variables represent ordered qualitative categories (e.g., mild, moderate, severe malnutrition). On the test paper, D is marked.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D (Categorical). Note: Scales of measurement: Nominal (labels), Ordinal (ordered ranks), Interval (equal intervals without absolute zero), Ratio (true zero).

cards.front: What is the term used to the monosaccharides and disaccharides added to foods and beverages by the manufacturer, cook or consumer, and these sugars naturally present in honey, syrups, fruit juices and fruit juice concentrates?
cards.rationale: The World Health Organization (WHO 2015 Guideline) defines 'Free sugars' as all monosaccharides and disaccharides added to foods and beverages by the manufacturer, cook, or consumer, plus sugars naturally present in honey, syrups, fruit juices, and fruit juice concentrates. WHO recommends free sugar intake be less than 10% (and ideally <5%) of total daily energy intake.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Intrinsic sugars (in whole fresh fruits/vegetables) and milk sugars (lactose) are NOT free sugars.

cards.front: Children put to the breast within 1 hour after birth is called
cards.rationale: WHO, UNICEF, and the Philippine Essential Intrapartum and Newborn Care (EINC / Unang Yakap) protocol define Early Initiation of Breastfeeding as putting the newborn to the mother's breast within the first hour of delivery. This ensures colostrum intake and stimulates maternal oxytocin/prolactin.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Early initiation: within 1 hour; Exclusive breastfeeding: breast milk only for 6 months; Continued breastfeeding: up to 2 years or beyond.

cards.front: This refers to the skills, supporting knowledge and professional values necessary to begin independent professional practice?
cards.rationale: Professional Competence refers to the integrated capability of applying foundational knowledge, clinical/technical skills, critical judgment, and ethical values required to perform health and nutrition services safely and independently.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Governed by PRC Professional Regulatory Board of Nutrition and Dietetics standards.

cards.front: The sustainable development goal considers ________ as an indicator of inadequate food intake and frequent attacks of illness.
cards.rationale: Historically under the MDGs (Target 1.C) and continued in SDG tracking frameworks, Underweight (low weight-for-age) serves as a classic composite indicator reflecting both acute food deprivation and recurrent infectious illnesses. (Note: Stunting reflects chronic deprivation, wasting reflects acute wasting).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B (underweight). Weight-for-age captures both chronic and acute insults.

cards.front: What is the measure that assess the benefits of interventions vis-a-vis cost?
cards.rationale: In health economics and program evaluation, cost-effectiveness analysis assesses the outcomes or benefits achieved relative to monetary costs expended. On the exam paper, option A is marked. In standard evaluation terminology, efficiency also assesses inputs/costs relative to outputs.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Margin handwritten note: '-> Face to face'. Cost-effectiveness weighs cost per unit of health benefit gained.

cards.front: Which of the following aims to improve current dietary practices to prevent diet-related public health problems in line with current scientific knowledge?
cards.rationale: The Nutritional Guidelines for Filipinos (NGF), revised by an inter-agency technical working group led by FNRI-DOST, is a set of primary dietary recommendations designed to foster healthy lifestyles, ensure nutritional adequacy, and prevent non-communicable diseases and nutritional deficiencies.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. NGF consists of 10 messages (10 Kumainments for popular advocacy).

cards.front: What is the IBW (in grams) of a 8 month - old infant who has a birth-weight of 2 kgs?
cards.rationale: Philippine pediatric nutrition formula for infant Ideal Body Weight (IBW): IBW (in g) = (Age in months * 500) + Birth Weight (in g). For an 8-month-old infant with birth weight 2000 g: IBW = (8 * 500) + 2000 = 4000 + 2000 = 6000 grams.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Margin calculations: '0-6 months - double', '7-12 months - triple', '13-24 months - quad'. Formula: IBW = (Age in mo * 500) + BW = (8 * 500) + 2000 = 6000 g.

cards.front: Determine which of the following nutrition intervention package addresses micronutrient supplementation in children at risk?
cards.back: Vitamin A supplementation between 6-59 months age
options: B. Supplementary feeding for moderate acute malnutrition
C. Calcium supplementation to mothers at-risk of low intake
D. Vitamin A supplementation between 6-59 months age
cards.rationale: Under the DOH National Micronutrient Supplementation Program (delivered via Garantisadong Pambata), universal and targeted Vitamin A Supplementation (VAS) of 100,000 IU for 6–11 months and 200,000 IU every 6 months for 12–59 months is the designated intervention package addressing micronutrient malnutrition in children.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Margin handwritten notes: '0-2 - 100k IU', '3-11 - 100k IU'. DOH VAS protocol: 6-11 mos = 100,000 IU (blue); 12-59 mos = 200,000 IU (red).

cards.front: What is your first step in developing your program plan?
options: C. Know and identify the problem
cards.rationale: The initial phase of any public health program planning process is situational analysis / problem identification to diagnose the community's nutritional issues, affected target populations, etiology, and severity.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Identical concept to Item 8. Planning begins with problem identification before formulating goals, strategies, or activities.

cards.front: The Administrative Order No. ________ embodies the strategic and operational framework for establishing integrated helminth control program.
cards.rationale: Department of Health Administrative Order No. 2006-0028 establishes the 'Strategic and Operational Framework for the Integrated Helminth Control Program (IHCP)' in the Philippines, targeting soil-transmitted helminthiasis (STH) through biannual mass drug administration (deworming) of children and pregnant women.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. DOH AO 2006-0028 = Integrated Helminth Control Program (IHCP).

cards.front: Which of these methods of nutritional assessment deals with the individual and measures objective criteria on a face - to - face mode?
cards.rationale: Direct nutritional assessment evaluates objective physiological, clinical, anthropometric, and biochemical criteria directly on individual subjects face-to-face, contrasting with indirect assessment which analyzes aggregated community indicators.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Direct assessment = individual face-to-face evaluation (ABCD methods).

cards.front: The Pres. Duterte's development pillars are: malasakit, pagbabago, and ________ and the vision of Ambisyon 2040.
cards.rationale: Under the Philippine Development Plan (PDP 2017–2022) anchored on AmBisyon Natin 2040, the national framework is structured around three strategic pillars: 1) Malasakit (Enhancing the Social Fabric), 2) Pagbabago (Inequality-Reducing Transformation), and 3) Patuloy na Pag-unlad / Kaunlaran (Increasing Growth Potential).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. PDP 2017-2022 pillars: Malasakit, Pagbabago, at Patuloy na Pag-unlad (Kaunlaran).

cards.front: Which of the following nutrients helps maintain muscle and body tissues?
cards.rationale: Dietary proteins provide the essential amino acids required for the synthesis, repair, and ongoing maintenance of skeletal muscle, vital organ tissues, collagen matrix, enzymes, and peptide hormones.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Proteins serve primarily structural and functional tissue maintenance roles.

cards.front: What is the step in program planning where the program manager will articulate what the program does and what to accomplish?
cards.rationale: Describing the program (program description/narrative) articulates the core mission, target population, structural components, specific activities, and what outcomes the program intends to accomplish.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Program description specifies what the program entails and the intended scope of results.

cards.front: Albendazole ________ mg is usually given to pregnant women during the 2nd trimester.
cards.rationale: Under WHO and Philippine DOH guidelines for pregnant women in soil-transmitted helminth (STH) endemic areas (>20% prevalence), a single oral dose of Albendazole 400 mg (or Mebendazole 500 mg) is administered after the first trimester (in the 2nd or 3rd trimester) to treat intestinal worms and prevent maternal anemia.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Albendazole dose: 400 mg single dose; contraindicated during the 1st trimester due to potential embryotoxicity.

cards.front: What is the type of study design in which it answers the question "what will happen" and it is a prospective observation of subjects?
cards.rationale: A prospective Cohort study follows a defined group of exposure-free individuals forward in time to observe incidence rates and determine 'what will happen' regarding disease or nutritional outcomes.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Margin notes: 'Cohort: exposure ng dalawang experiment... walang disease ung isa may disease', 'Cross-sectional: data na paghahambingin', 'Case series: 2 o series ng case study na pinagtugma'.

cards.front: During lactation the additional daily energy requirement is ________
cards.rationale: According to the Philippine Dietary Reference Intakes (PDRI 2015), the additional daily energy allowance during the first six months of exclusive lactation is +500 kcal/day (to support human milk synthesis yielding ~750–800 ml/day). In pregnancy (2nd/3rd trimester), the additional energy is +300 kcal/day.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Margin handwritten note next to A: 'pregnant'. Lactation allowance = +500 kcal/day; Pregnancy allowance = +300 kcal/day.

cards.front: Which of the following are you going to use to answer the question of how much you should eat in one meal in order to be healthy?
cards.rationale: Pinggang Pinoy, developed by FNRI-DOST in collaboration with DOH and WHO, is an intuitive visual food guide specifically designed to demonstrate recommended food group proportions and portion sizes per single meal (half plate Glow foods: fruits and vegetables; one-quarter Grow foods: protein; one-quarter Go foods: carbohydrates). The Food Pyramid depicts daily food choices.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Pinggang Pinoy = PER MEAL food guide; Food Pyramid = DAILY food guide.

cards.front: What is the act of conducting systematic appraisal of the success of a program?
cards.rationale: Evaluation is the systematic and objective assessment of the design, implementation, and overall success or impact of an ongoing or completed public health initiative.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Appraisal of success/worth/impact = Evaluation. Tracking day-to-day progress = Monitoring.

cards.front: When do you give iron-folic acid supplements in malaria endemic areas?
options: D. Simultaneous with screening/treatment of malaria
cards.rationale: Under WHO guidelines for malaria-endemic areas, iron and folic acid supplementation should be integrated alongside active screening, prevention (bed nets, vector control), and prompt antimalarial treatment. Option A is marked on the examination paper.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Margin handwritten note: 'iron ay kakainin ni malaria' (referring to how Plasmodium parasites utilize host iron, hence the necessity of concurrent screening/treatment).

cards.front: When is the period of second growth spurt?
cards.rationale: Human postnatal physical growth exhibits two major rapid velocity spurts: the first occurs during infancy (first year of life), and the second occurs during adolescence (the pubertal growth spurt driven by sex steroids and growth hormone).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Margin handwritten note: '1st menarche - bago mag dalaga'. 1st growth spurt = infancy; 2nd growth spurt = adolescence.

cards.front: Which of the following is the guide for all who want to be involved in nutrition action because it lays out targets, directions, and priority actions, among others?
options: D. Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition
cards.rationale: On the candidate's examination paper, option A ('Sustainable Development Goals') is circled. In Philippine national policy, the Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition (PPAN, Option D) is the comprehensive national multi-sectoral blueprint that articulates precise targets, directions, and priority nutrition actions.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A (Sustainable Development Goals). Note: Both SDGs (global) and PPAN (national) lay out targets and priority actions; examinee marked A.

cards.front: What is the term used to describe the complex disorder involving an excessive amount of body fat?
cards.rationale: Obesity is medically and epidemiologically defined as a chronic, complex relapsing non-communicable disease characterized by abnormal or excessive accumulation of body fat (adiposity) that impairs physical and metabolic health.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Repeated verbatim as Item 80 in this exam.

cards.front: The long range direction that answers the question of what you must focus on to achieve the vision is ________
cards.rationale: In strategic management and program planning, the Mission defines the fundamental purpose, scope of operations, and core operational focus of an organization or program—answering what must be done to attain the long-term Vision.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Repeated verbatim as Item 165 in this exam. Vision = what we want to become; Mission = what we do/focus on to get there.

cards.front: What R.A was enacted in Year 2016 to promote and upgrade the practice of the professionals in the country?
cards.rationale: Republic Act No. 10912 is the 'Continuing Professional Development (CPD) Act of 2016', enacted on July 21, 2016. It mandates continuing education and credit units for the renewal of Professional Identification Cards across all regulated professions under the PRC.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. RA 10912 = Continuing Professional Development (CPD) Act of 2016.

cards.front: What is the type of study in which the effect of a given treatment is observed and assessed?
cards.rationale: In an Experimental study design (such as a randomized clinical trial or community intervention trial), the investigator deliberately manipulates or assigns the independent variable (treatment/intervention) and observes the outcome effects.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Experimental studies actively intervene/treat; observational studies merely observe without manipulation.

cards.front: What are the different contaminants of foods?
cards.rationale: Under food safety science and HACCP principles, food hazards and contaminants are classically classified into three major categories: 1) Biological/microbiological (bacteria, viruses, parasites), 2) Chemical (pesticides, toxins, heavy metals), and 3) Physical (glass, metal fragments, stones, bone splinters).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. The classic triad of food safety hazards: Biological/microbiological, Chemical, and Physical.

cards.front: What is the process of 'working collaboratively with relevant partners who share common goals and interests' or 'working collaboratively with and for groups of people affiliated by geographical proximity, special interest, or similar situations to address issues on nutrition and well-being of people'?
cards.rationale: Community engagement / community participation is the process of working collaboratively with and through groups of people affiliated by geographic proximity, special interest, or shared circumstances to address issues affecting their health, nutrition, and well-being.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B (top of page 6). Emphasizes authentic partnership, community ownership, and empowering local stakeholders.

cards.front: The proportion of children 6 to 23 months meeting both the minimum meal frequency to ensure both dietary and nutrient adequacy is ________
cards.rationale: In WHO/UNICEF Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) indicators, the Minimum Acceptable Diet (MAD) is a composite indicator measuring the proportion of children 6–23 months of age who receive both the minimum dietary diversity (consuming foods from >= 5 of 8 food groups) and minimum meal frequency.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. MAD = Minimum Dietary Diversity (MDD) + Minimum Meal Frequency (MMF).

cards.front: What is the measure of detecting early changes in body metabolism & nutrition before the appearance of overt clinical signs?
cards.rationale: Biochemical assessment (laboratory measurement of nutrients, metabolites, or enzyme cofactors in blood, urine, or tissue) detects subclinical nutrient depletion and cellular metabolic alterations long before physical signs or anatomical growth deficits emerge.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Repeated verbatim as Item 130 in this exam. Sequence of deficiency: Dietary inadequacy -> Decreased tissue stores -> Biochemical lesion -> Clinical signs.

cards.front: Maternal ________ is associated with overweight babies at birth.
cards.rationale: Pre-pregnancy maternal obesity and excessive gestational weight gain increase fetal glucose exposure and hyperinsulinemia (Pedersen hypothesis), leading to macrosomia (birth weight > 4,000 g) and large-for-gestational-age (LGA) infants.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Maternal obesity -> fetal macrosomia / LGA; Maternal undernutrition/iron deficiency -> low birth weight / SGA.

cards.front: After the age of 59, caloric requirements is generally ________
cards.rationale: In older adults (> 59 years), resting metabolic rate decreases by approximately 2–3% per decade due to progressive age-related loss of lean skeletal muscle mass (sarcopenia) and concurrent reduction in voluntary physical activity, leading to lower total daily caloric requirements.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Caloric needs decrease in elderly adults, but micronutrient density requirements (protein, calcium, vitamin D, B12) remain high.

cards.front: Megaloblastic anemia is caused by ________ deficiency/deficiencies.
cards.rationale: Megaloblastic anemia is characterized by large, immature nucleated erythroblasts in the bone marrow caused by impaired thymidylate and DNA synthesis due to deficiency of Folic Acid (Vitamin B9) or Vitamin B12 (cobalamin). Iron deficiency causes microcytic hypochromic anemia.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Margin handwritten notes: 'megaloblastic', 'B12 Cobalamin pernicious', 'Iron - Microcytic'. Folic acid/B12 = Megaloblastic; Iron = Microcytic.

cards.front: The transition in an infant's diet from breastmilk to other sources of foods is called ________
cards.rationale: Complementary Feeding is the recommended term describing the period starting at 6 months when breast milk alone is no longer sufficient to meet nutritional requirements, and other solid/semi-solid foods are introduced alongside continued breastfeeding.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Modern public health nutrition emphasizes 'complementary feeding' rather than 'weaning' to reinforce that breast milk should continue alongside solid foods.

cards.front: What period after birth is considered as exclusively breastfed?
cards.rationale: WHO, UNICEF, and the Philippine Department of Health recommend exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months of life (0 to 180 days). During this period, the infant receives only breast milk, with no other liquids or solids, not even water (with the exception of oral rehydration salts, vitamins, minerals, and medicines).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Exclusive breastfeeding duration = first 6 months (0-180 days).

cards.front: This pertains to a public health nutritionist who has communication skills, ranging from writing professional reports to the development of health and nutrition information that is inclusive and appropriate to target populations with appropriate financial management system.
cards.rationale: The Administrator role in public health nutrition encompasses comprehensive executive leadership, program communication, strategic technical reporting, stakeholder coordination, and fiscal/financial resource management systems.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Financial management combined with strategic professional communication defines the Public Health Nutrition Administrator.

cards.front: What is the tool needed to be developed in order to have a clearer overview of the objectives, the possible causal factors, and related data that will aid the RND in identifying relevant indicators to be collected for program proposal?
cards.rationale: A Causal Model (problem tree or UNICEF conceptual framework of malnutrition) maps the immediate, underlying, and basic determinants of nutritional problems. It provides a visual schematic connecting causes to outcomes, guiding program planners in selecting target intervention points and measurable indicators.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Causal models/problem trees structure the logical linkages between root causes and health indicators.

cards.front: What period after birth does infant receives colostrum from the mother?
cards.rationale: Colostrum is secreted immediately following birth and is richest during the first 24 hours postpartum. Timely feeding within 24 hours delivers high concentrations of antibodies, lactoferrin, and oligosaccharides essential for gut protection.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Colostrum is immediately available and transferred during early skin-to-skin suckling within 24 hours.

cards.front: What is that document that outlines the decisions of the government to control malnutrition through the various sectors, indicating the precise objectives, targets and plan of action of each sector over a given time frame?
cards.rationale: A National Nutrition Policy (or strategic national nutrition plan such as the PPAN) represents the official multi-sectoral government statement and commitment detailing overarching targets, sectoral responsibilities, and specific strategic frameworks to eliminate malnutrition over a specified timeframe.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Nutrition Policy sets the binding inter-sectoral government priorities and goals.

cards.front: The birth weight of an infant is dependent on ________
options: A. fat intake of the mother
cards.rationale: Maternal nutritional status—encompassing pre-pregnancy body mass index, micronutrient stores, and appropriate gestational weight gain throughout pregnancy—is the foremost modifiable determinant of fetal growth and birth weight.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Maternal nutrition directly governs placental nutrient transport and fetal intrauterine accretion.

cards.front: Which of the following agencies, as member of the NNC Board, that implements the research programs as basis for program planning?
cards.rationale: The Department of Science and Technology (DOST), through its attached research agency the Food and Nutrition Research Institute (FNRI-DOST), conducts the periodic National Nutrition Surveys (Expanded National Nutrition Survey / ENNS), generating empirical scientific data that forms the basis for national nutrition planning.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. DOST/FNRI = research and national nutrition surveys; DA = agriculture/food security; DOH = lead chair agency.

cards.front: What is the basic principle in planning that pertains to specific activities and must all be implemented contributing to the achievement of the objectives?
cards.rationale: The planning principle of Comprehensiveness dictates that all relevant intervention components, complementary activities, support systems, and resource requirements are systematically incorporated into the program design so they work synergistically toward achieving the objectives.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Comprehensiveness ensures all interrelated actions required to meet the objectives are included in the plan.

cards.front: What is a marker of suboptimal intrauterine growth and poor maternal nutrition; it increases the risks for poorer outcomes in growth, development and health in both the short and the long term?
cards.rationale: Low Birth Weight (LBW, defined as birth weight < 2,500 grams) is a primary marker of intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) and/or preterm birth. LBW significantly elevates infant mortality risk, childhood stunting, and the developmental origins of adult chronic disease (Barker hypothesis).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. LBW (< 2500 g) is the clinical marker of poor intrauterine growth and maternal undernutrition.

cards.front: A birth weight below the 10th percentile for gestational age based on a reference population is ________
cards.rationale: Small-for-Gestational-Age (SGA) is clinically and epidemiologically defined as a birth weight below the 10th percentile for sex and specific completed weeks of gestational age, distinguishing infants with pathological fetal growth restriction from those born early but appropriately sized.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. SGA = birth weight < 10th percentile for gestational age. Low birth weight = < 2500 g regardless of gestational age.

cards.front: The techniques that enhance learning among older adults is called ________
cards.rationale: Geragogy (or eldergogy) refers specifically to the instructional methodologies and educational strategies tailored to the cognitive, sensory, and psychosocial learning needs of older adults (the elderly). Pedagogy refers to teaching children, and andragogy refers to teaching adults in general.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Margin handwritten notes: 'geriatric' next to Geragogy, 'adult' next to Andragogy, 'children' next to Pedagogy.

cards.front: Which of the following is one of the major activities in the identification of the causal causes of the nutritional problems?
cards.back: Identification of the causes of the problem
options: A. Identification of the causes of the problem
cards.rationale: In situational analysis and causal analysis (such as constructing a problem tree), systematically identifying immediate, underlying, and root causes is the core analytical activity that determines why the nutritional problem exists.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Causal analysis diagnoses 'why' malnutrition occurs in the target population.

cards.front: What is the measure that reflects body composition such as body fat and lean body mass, and is considered a more accurate indicator than height/weight tables?
cards.rationale: Body Mass Index (BMI = weight in kg / height in m2) is an anthropometric index of weight adjusted for height that correlates closely with total body fatness and adiposity-related health risks across adult populations, offering a standardized measure superior to simple height-weight tables.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. BMI is the universal screening index for adult nutritional status and adiposity.

cards.front: In anthropometric measurement, a combination of an index and a cut-off is called ________
cards.rationale: In nutritional epidemiology: A raw measurement is an unadjusted value (e.g., weight); an Index is a combination of two measurements or a measurement and age (e.g., weight-for-height); an Indicator is an index combined with a predefined statistical cut-off point used to classify or estimate prevalence (e.g., WFH < -2 SD defines the indicator of wasting).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Margin handwritten note: 'indicator - index + cut-off'. Measurement -> Index -> Indicator.

cards.front: What is the important nutrient that is needed in protein, RNA, and DNA synthesis, cell division, and differentiation?
cards.rationale: Zinc is an essential trace element required as a structural and catalytic component of over 300 metalloenzymes, including RNA polymerases, DNA polymerases, and zinc-finger transcription factors that regulate gene expression, cell division, and cellular differentiation.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Zinc is critical for nucleic acid synthesis, cellular proliferation, wound healing, and immune defense.

cards.front: What is the main category of research in which subjects are looked over or are being watched?
cards.rationale: Observational research encompasses study designs (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) wherein investigators passively observe exposures, behaviors, and health outcomes in study participants without introducing clinical interventions or experimental manipulations.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Observational = observing naturally occurring events; Experimental = actively assigning treatments.

cards.front: The desirable weight gain during pregnancy is ________ kgs.
cards.rationale: Institute of Medicine (IOM) and Philippine maternal guidelines recommend total gestational weight gain based on pre-pregnancy BMI: for underweight women (BMI < 18.5), recommended gain is 12.5 to 18.0 kg (averaging around 16–17 kg). On this exam paper, B (16.8 kg) is marked.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B (16.8). Note standard IOM ranges: Underweight: 12.5-18 kg; Normal: 11.5-16 kg; Overweight: 7-11.5 kg; Obese: 5-9 kg.

cards.front: The basal metabolic rate during pregnancy is increased by ________ % by the end of the term.
cards.rationale: By the late third trimester of pregnancy, maternal Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) increases by roughly 20% to 25% due to the metabolic demands of the growing fetus, placental active transport, expanded maternal circulatory volume, and increased uterine and cardiac workload.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D (20 to 25). Repeated as Item 79 where option B (20 to 25) was marked.

cards.front: Which of the following are the pillars of the sustainable development goals?
cards.rationale: The United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) framework is founded upon three interdependent, mutually reinforcing pillars of sustainable development: Economic Growth/Development, Social Inclusion/Development, and Environmental Protection/Sustainability.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. The 3 SDG pillars: Economic, Social, and Environmental dimensions.

cards.front: What is the practice of adding an essential micronutrient in a food to improve the nutritional quality and provide a public health benefit with minimal risk to health.
cards.rationale: According to the Codex Alimentarius and WHO/FAO guidelines, Food Fortification is the practice of deliberately increasing the content of an essential micronutrient in a food vehicle to improve nutritional quality and provide a public health benefit with minimal health risk.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. In the Philippines, governed by RA 8976 (Food Fortification Act of 2000).

cards.front: The ________ mg daily calcium requirement for adolescents is the same for boys and girls.
cards.rationale: According to the Philippine Dietary Reference Intakes (PDRI 2015), the Recommended Energy and Nutrient Intake (RENI) for calcium for adolescents aged 10–18 years is 1000 mg/day for both boys and girls to optimize peak bone mass accretion during pubertal growth.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Adolescent calcium requirement in PDRI is 1000 mg/day for both sexes.

cards.front: The basal metabolic rate during pregnancy is increased by ________ % by the end of the term.
cards.rationale: Maternal basal metabolic rate rises progressively over gestation, peaking in the third trimester at an elevation of 20% to 25% above pre-pregnancy baseline.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Exact duplicate of Item 75 testing third-trimester BMR elevation.

cards.front: What is the term used to describe the complex disorder involving an excessive amount of body fat?
cards.rationale: Obesity is a complex multifactorial disease characterized by excess adiposity resulting from prolonged positive energy balance, predisposing individuals to cardiovascular, endocrine, and metabolic comorbidities.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Verbatim repeat of Item 46.

cards.front: After birth, fetal iron storage is still sufficient until the period of ________ months.
cards.rationale: Full-term healthy newborns possess hepatic iron stores accumulated during late pregnancy that satisfy erythropoiesis and tissue requirements for the first 4 to 6 months of life. Beyond 6 months, iron stores deplete, necessitating iron-rich complementary foods.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Fetal iron stores last 4-6 months in term infants (shorter in preterm/LBW infants: 2-3 months).

cards.front: The implementation of planned and systematic activities necessary to ensure that products or services meet quality standards is ________
cards.rationale: Quality Assurance (QA) comprises planned, systematic operational and managerial activities implemented within a quality system to provide adequate confidence that health and nutrition services or products satisfy stated standards.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Quality assurance establishes protocols and compliance checks to maintain quality standards.

cards.front: Serum calcium, are tightly controlled metabolically and are poor reflections of dietary intake or nutritional status. This statement is ________
cards.rationale: This statement is TRUE. Serum ionized and total calcium concentrations are maintained within strict homeostatic limits (8.5–10.5 mg/dL) by parathyroid hormone (PTH), calcitonin, and calcitriol acting on bone resorption and renal reabsorption. Consequently, serum calcium levels do not reflect dietary calcium intake or bone mineral density.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C (true). Serum calcium reflects homeostatic endocrine regulation, NOT dietary calcium adequacy.

cards.front: A LBW infant may need to catch up ________ fold increase in weight to have optimal growth.
cards.rationale: Low birth weight (LBW) infants undergo rapid compensatory catch-up growth during the first year of life, frequently quadrupling (4-fold increase) their birth weight by 12 months to converge toward normal developmental centiles.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C (4). Notice duplicate item appears as Item 121 where option D (4) was marked.

cards.front: Which of these refers to the set of interrelated projects that presents personnel, facilities, budget, equipment and supplies and other items directed to accomplish specific goals and objectives?
cards.rationale: A Program is an organized portfolio of interrelated projects and ongoing activities coordinated with institutional resources (personnel, budget, facilities, equipment) to achieve broad, long-range strategic goals and objectives.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Hierarchy: Policy -> Plan -> Program -> Project -> Activity.

cards.front: The average increase in height of infants during the first year of life is ________ cm.
cards.rationale: During the first year of life, an infant's length increases substantially from an average birth length of ~50 cm to ~74–75 cm, representing an increment of approximately 24 to 25 cm. On the examination paper, option A (21 to 24 cm) is marked.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Margin handwritten notes: 'pag 1 yr - hanggang 24 cm', 'pag 2 yrs - 12 cm', 'pag 3 yrs - 8 cm', '4-8 yrs - 5 to 6 cm'.

cards.front: In statistics, the number that occurs most often within a set of number is called the ________
cards.rationale: In descriptive statistics, the Mode is the measure of central tendency defined as the value or category that appears with the greatest frequency in a distribution.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Mean = arithmetic average; Median = middle value (50th percentile); Mode = most frequent value.

cards.front: The document that details for implementation of the action plan; specific projects are defined is called ________
cards.rationale: An Action Plan is an operational document that outlines the specific tasks, timelines, responsibilities, resource allocations, and operational procedures necessary to implement strategic objectives and programs.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Action plans translate high-level strategies into actionable operational schedules.

cards.front: The proportion for breastfed and non-breastfed children 6 to 23 months who receives solid, semi-solid, or soft foods consumed at the minimum number of times per day.
cards.rationale: Minimum Meal Frequency (MMF) is a core WHO/UNICEF IYCF indicator measuring the proportion of breastfed and non-breastfed children 6–23 months who receive solid, semi-solid, or soft foods (plus milk feeds for non-breastfed) at or above minimum age-specific frequencies (2 times for 6-8 mos, 3 times for 9-23 mos breastfed; 4 times for non-breastfed).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. MMF measures feeding frequency/quantity; MDD measures dietary quality/diversity.

cards.front: The condition when "all people, at all times, have physical, social and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food which meets their dietary needs and food preferences for an active and healthy life" is termed as ________ security.
cards.rationale: This is the universal definition of Food Security adopted at the 1996 World Food Summit by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). It rests on four pillars: availability, access, utilization, and stability.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. FAO 1996 World Food Summit definition of Food Security.

cards.front: What is the term given when planning is done at the national level?
cards.rationale: Macro-level planning refers to high-level strategic, policy, and budgetary planning conducted at the central or national level (e.g., national development plans, PPAN), whereas micro-level planning occurs at local, municipal, or community levels.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Macro-level = national/central; Meso-level = regional/provincial; Micro-level = community/barangay.

cards.front: STATISTICS is the science of conducting studies to.......
cards.back: collect, organize, summarize, analyze, and draw conclusions from data
options: A. monitor, study, and report on a subject.
B. solve a system of equations
C. hypothesize, experiment, and form conclusions
D. collect, organize, summarize, analyze, and draw conclusions from data
cards.rationale: Statistics is formally defined as the scientific discipline concerned with designing studies, and collecting, organizing, presenting, analyzing, and drawing valid inferences and conclusions from numerical data.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Standard comprehensive textbook definition of statistics.

cards.front: The NNC Governing Board has ________ members who are the Secretaries of different government agencies.
cards.rationale: Under Executive Order No. 234 and Executive Order No. 472, the National Nutrition Council (NNC) Governing Board includes the heads/Secretaries of 10 key government departments: DOH (Chair), DA (Vice Chair), DILG (Vice Chair), DepEd, DSWD, DOST, DBM, NEDA, DTI, and DOLE, alongside 3 private sector representatives.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. NNC Governing Board contains 10 Department Secretaries as government agency members.

cards.front: What are the interventions that address the underlying determinants of foetal and child nutrition and development?
cards.rationale: According to the Lancet Commission on Maternal and Child Nutrition and the PPAN: Nutrition-sensitive interventions address the underlying determinants of malnutrition (food security, agriculture, safe water, sanitation, female education, social safety nets); Nutrition-specific interventions address immediate causes (adequate food intake, disease control, micronutrient feeding).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Margin handwritten note next to D: 'immediate cause'. Nutrition-sensitive = underlying determinants; Nutrition-specific = immediate determinants.

cards.front: What is the daily fluid intake (in ml) of an infant weighing 1000 grams?
cards.rationale: In neonatal fluid calculation questions from PRC board examinations, option D (800 to 850 ml or scaled volume per body weight category) is marked on the test paper.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D (800 to 850). Note: Preterm infant maintenance fluid protocols require meticulous titration based on daily weight and renal status.

cards.front: That which inhibits intracellular viral replication is called
cards.rationale: Interferons (IFN-alpha, IFN-beta, IFN-gamma) are cytokine glycoproteins synthesized and secreted by virus-infected cells. They bind to neighboring cell surface receptors, inducing an antiviral state and activating protein kinase R (PKR) and 2',5'-oligoadenylate synthetase, which directly degrades viral RNA and inhibits intracellular viral protein translation.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Interferons inhibit intracellular viral replication; lactoferrin sequesters iron; lysozyme lyses bacterial peptidoglycan walls.

cards.front: The adolescent growth spurt in boys begins between the ages of ________ years.
cards.rationale: The adolescent pubertal growth spurt in boys typically commences between ages 12 and 14 years, peaking between 14 and 16 years (Tanner stage 3–4), which is approximately two years later than in girls (who spurt between ages 10 and 14).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Boys spurt later (12-16 years) and gain greater lean body mass than girls.

cards.front: It pertains to targeted activities in individuals or groups with early signs of disease to prevent progression
cards.rationale: Early Intervention (corresponding to secondary prevention in public health) involves detecting early, subclinical, or initial pathological signs and delivering prompt targeted clinical and nutritional therapies to halt disease progression and prevent permanent complications.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Early Intervention = secondary prevention halting progression of identified early signs.

cards.front: What is the R.A. that was enacted and is known as the "Kalusugan at Nutrisyon ng Mag-Nanay Act"?
cards.rationale: Republic Act No. 11148, enacted on November 29, 2018, is officially known as the 'Kalusugan at Nutrisyon ng Mag-Nanay Act'. It scales up maternal and child nutrition programs across the First 1,000 Days of life (from conception up to the child's second birthday) to end stunting and malnutrition.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. RA 11148 = Kalusugan at Nutrisyon ng Mag-Nanay Act (First 1,000 Days Law). Landmark legislation in Philippine nutrition.

cards.front: The researcher want to collect incidence of hypertension in the community. What survey method is to be employed?
cards.rationale: Determining blood pressure status and detecting new cases of hypertension requires direct physiological measurement using standardized, calibrated sphygmomanometers and blood pressure cuffs, as self-reports or interviews are notoriously prone to recall and diagnostic misclassification.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Clinical objective diagnoses like hypertension require direct physiological measurement.

cards.front: This is considered as a healthy weight range as per BMI WHO Classification
cards.rationale: Under the WHO International Classification for adult Body Mass Index (BMI): Underweight = < 18.5 kg/m2; Normal / Healthy Weight = 18.5 to 24.9 kg/m2; Overweight = 25.0 to 29.9 kg/m2; Obese = >= 30.0 kg/m2. (Note: Asian cut-offs define normal as 18.5–22.9 kg/m2).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. WHO international normal weight standard = 18.5–24.9 kg/m2.

cards.front: The period characterized by slowing down of growth and body changes occur gradually is ________
cards.rationale: The school-age period (middle childhood, ages 6 to 12 years) is characterized by a latent, steady, and gradual rate of linear growth and weight gain (average 2–3 kg and 5–6 cm per year), in contrast to the rapid acceleration observed in infancy and pubertal adolescence.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. School-age childhood = steady, gradual latent growth between the two major growth spurts.

cards.front: The study of the distribution and determinants of health-related states or events in specified populations, and the application of this study to the control of health problems is ________
cards.rationale: This is John M. Last's definitive and globally recognized definition of Epidemiology, adopted by the WHO, CDC, and public health curricula worldwide.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Margin handwritten note: 'control of disease'. Classic definition of Epidemiology.

cards.front: During pregnancy the major adjustment in energy utilization is a shift in fuel source where ________ is the major fetal fuel.
cards.rationale: During pregnancy, maternal endocrine changes (placental lactogen, progesterone) induce mild maternal peripheral insulin resistance, sparing glucose for rapid facilitated diffusion across the placenta via GLUT-1 transporters. D-Glucose (carbohydrate) is the primary obligatory metabolic fuel for fetal oxidative metabolism.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Maternal metabolism shifts to fat oxidation to spare glucose (carbohydrates) for the growing fetus.

cards.front: The integral part of the Philippine Development Plan 2017-2022 which is a results-based plan with SMART results at different levels is the
cards.back: Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition
options: A. Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition
D. Development Plan of the Philippines
cards.rationale: The Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition (PPAN 2017–2022) serves as the designated sectoral plan for nutrition integrated directly into the Philippine Development Plan (PDP 2017–2022), framing results-based SMART indicators to accelerate reduction of stunting and wasting.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. PPAN 2017-2022 is the results-based nutrition blueprint within the PDP.

cards.front: What is the act that attempts to bring together the widest possible range of inter-sector allies to raise awareness and participation for the convergence of resources rather than with specific behaviour change?
cards.rationale: Social Mobilization is defined as a broad-scale participatory process that rallies multiple societal sectors, community organizations, policymakers, and civic allies to pool institutional resources, build public momentum, and create an enabling environment for social change.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Social mobilization engages intersectoral allies and pools resources; social marketing focuses on individual behavior change.

cards.front: The wide variety of activities to "sell" the products, ideas or concepts that involves media and interpersonal channels is ________
cards.rationale: In the classic 4 Ps of social marketing (Product, Price, Place, Promotion), Promotion encompasses the diverse range of advertising, public relations, mass media broadcasts, community outreach, and interpersonal communication strategies used to raise awareness and persuade target audiences.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. The 4 Ps of social marketing: Product, Price, Place, and Promotion.

cards.front: When year was the Food Fortification Law of the Philippines enacted?
cards.rationale: Republic Act No. 8976, known as the 'Philippine Food Fortification Act of 2000', was signed into law on November 7, 2000. It instituted mandatory fortification of staple foods (rice with iron, wheat flour with iron and vitamin A, cooking oil and refined sugar with vitamin A).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. RA 8976 enacted in 2000. Mandates fortification of staples and voluntary Sangkap Pinoy seal.

cards.front: Maternal ________ is associated with babies with low weight (<2500 g) at birth.
cards.rationale: Maternal iron deficiency and iron-deficiency anemia in pregnancy impair uteroplacental perfusion, oxygenation, and tissue synthesis, significantly increasing the clinical risk of intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), low birth weight (< 2,500 g), and preterm birth.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Contrast with Item 54: Maternal iron deficiency -> LBW; Maternal obesity -> overweight/macrosomic baby.

cards.front: During the first year, infants increase their height by ________ %.
cards.rationale: An infant's average birth length is approximately 50 cm. By 12 months (1 year) of age, the infant reaches an average length of approximately 75 cm. This represents a 25 cm increase, or exactly a 50% increase over birth length.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. First year linear growth: 50 cm at birth -> 75 cm at 1 year = 50% increase in length. (Weight triples, or increases ~200%).

cards.front: After birth, fetal iron storage diminishes during the period ________ months.
cards.rationale: Endogenous neonatal hepatic iron stores established in utero sustain blood volume expansion and tissue growth until 4 to 6 months of age, after which iron stores diminish and dietary complementary foods become imperative.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Fetal iron storage diminishes between 4 and 6 months postpartum.

cards.front: Anemia is caused by ________ deficiency/deficiencies. (select the best answer)
cards.rationale: While folate, B12, and protein deficiencies can cause specific forms of anemia, iron deficiency accounts for approximately 50% or more of all anemia cases globally and is the single most prevalent nutritional deficiency worldwide. On the examination paper, option A (iron) is circled as the best answer.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A (iron). Note: Iron is the primary etiology of nutritional anemia; 'select the best answer' directs to iron.

cards.front: What is the factor in food choices that relates to policies on agricultural subsidies, trade regulations and taxes that enhances individual's financial capacity to obtain foods?
cards.rationale: Economic access/accessibility refers to whether individuals and households have the purchasing power and financial resources to acquire adequate foods, heavily influenced by fiscal policies, agricultural pricing, subsidies, and trade tariffs. On the exam paper, option B (Accessibility) is circled.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B (Accessibility). Economic accessibility relates directly to purchasing power and food price policies.

cards.front: The products intended to address the nutrients gap that contain one or more dietary ingredients is called ________
cards.rationale: Dietary Supplements are manufactured products intended to supplement the daily diet and address nutritional gaps, formulated to contain one or more dietary ingredients such as vitamins, minerals, herbs, amino acids, or enzymes in concentrated dosage forms.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Dietary supplements bridge nutrient gaps with concentrated vitamins, minerals, or amino acids.

cards.front: The WHO recommendation for daily fruit and vegetable intake is ________ grams.
cards.rationale: The World Health Organization (WHO) and FAO recommend a minimum consumption of 400 grams (equivalent to five servings of 80 grams each) of fruits and vegetables per day (excluding starchy tubers like potatoes and cassava) to prevent chronic non-communicable diseases.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. WHO target = minimum 400 grams/day of fruits and vegetables (5 servings).

cards.front: How many indicators are contained in the MDG?
cards.rationale: The Millennium Development Goals (MDGs, 2000–2015) were structured around 8 overarching Goals. On the examination paper, option C (8) is circled, with a margin note clarifying 'eight goals'. (Technically, the MDG monitoring framework contained 8 goals, 21 targets, and 60 official indicators).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C (8). Margin handwritten note: 'eight goals'. The question loosely asks for indicators but options correspond to the 8 MDG goals.

cards.front: Which of the following lays out targets, directions, and priority actions in 2030?
options: D. Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition
cards.rationale: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, adopted by all UN Member States in 2015, establishes the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) with 169 targets to guide global and national priority actions and policies through the year 2030.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. The 2030 global development horizon belongs to the UN Sustainable Development Goals.

cards.front: What is the type of monosaccharides that provides energy to the brain?
cards.rationale: D-Glucose is the obligate and primary metabolic monosaccharide fuel utilized by the human brain under normal non-fasting physiological conditions, crossing the blood-brain barrier via GLUT-1 transporters to support neuronal oxidative phosphorylation.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Glucose is the primary fuel for the brain and red blood cells.

cards.front: The Maternal, Neonatal and Child Health and Nutrition guidelines states that the third pre-natal visit of a pregnant woman must be on the ________ weeks.
cards.rationale: Under the DOH Maternal, Neonatal, and Child Health and Nutrition (MNCHN) strategy, pregnant women must receive a minimum of four antenatal care (ANC) visits: 1st visit in 1st trimester (<12 weeks); 2nd visit in 2nd trimester (around 24–28 weeks); 3rd visit in early 3rd trimester (around 32 weeks); and 4th visit in late 3rd trimester (around 36–38 weeks).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. DOH 4-visit ANC schedule: 1st visit = 1st trimester; 2nd = 2nd trimester (~24-28 wks); 3rd = 32nd week; 4th = 36-38 weeks.

cards.front: What is the type of study in which the researcher collects data at one point in time?
cards.rationale: A Cross-sectional study (also known as a prevalence study) collects exposure and outcome data from a defined population simultaneously at a single specific point in time, providing a 'snapshot' of community nutritional status.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Cross-sectional = data collected at a single point in time (prevalence snapshot).

cards.front: A LBW infants may need to catch up ________ fold increase in weight to have optimal growth.
cards.rationale: Low birth weight (LBW) infants generally require compensatory accelerated growth during infancy, typically reaching a four-fold (4-fold) increase in their initial birth weight by 12 months to achieve appropriate growth percentiles.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D (4). Reiteration of Item 84 testing the 4-fold weight increase required for LBW catch-up.

cards.front: What is the indicator to assess the severity of Vitamin A deficiency in most age groups in the population?
cards.rationale: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), subclinical Vitamin A Deficiency (VAD) is defined by a serum or plasma retinol concentration of less than 0.70 umol/L (or < 20 ug/dL). A population prevalence of serum retinol < 0.70 umol/L of >= 15% signifies a severe public health problem.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. WHO cutoff: Serum retinol < 0.70 umol/L (< 20 ug/dL) defines Vitamin A deficiency.

cards.front: How many indicators are contained in the Sustainable Development Goals?
cards.rationale: The United Nations 2030 Agenda consists of 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Although the monitoring framework includes 169 targets and 232 official statistical indicators, board exam questions frequently refer to the 17 headline goals.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C (17). Corresponds to the 17 SDG Goals (Goal 2 = Zero Hunger).

cards.front: Food choices at the communal and individual level are influenced by ________
cards.rationale: Food choices and dietary consumption patterns are determined by a complex interplay of environmental and economic factors, notably physical food availability in the market, geographical accessibility, and economic affordability/purchasing power.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. All three elements (availability, accessibility, affordability) govern community food choices.

cards.front: The addition of a nutrient to a food vehicle commonly consumed by the population to prevent or correct a micronutrient deficiency is ________
cards.rationale: Under RA 8976 and WHO/FAO standards, Food Fortification is the addition of essential micronutrients (e.g. vitamin A, iron, iodine) to widely consumed staple foods (food vehicles) to prevent or correct population-wide nutritional deficiencies.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Food Fortification adds micronutrients to staple vehicles to correct population deficiencies.

cards.front: The activities that aim to prevent diseases in populations before they occur is ________
cards.rationale: Primary Prevention intervenes before the onset of disease or pathological changes occur, through health promotion, immunization, universal food fortification, clean water/sanitation, and dietary education to eliminate underlying risk factors.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Primary prevention = prevents disease before occurrence; Secondary = early screening/treatment; Tertiary = rehabilitation.

cards.front: During pregnancy the additional daily water requirement is ________ ml.
cards.rationale: According to the Philippine Dietary Reference Intakes (PDRI 2015) and maternal nutrition guidelines, pregnant women require an additional fluid intake of approximately 300 ml/day (about 1 additional cup/glass of water) to support blood volume expansion, amniotic fluid, and fetal circulation.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Pregnancy requires +300 ml/day additional water; Lactation requires +700-1000 ml/day.

cards.front: A concrete definition of the major steps taken by an organization to achieve its mission and vision is termed as ________
cards.rationale: In strategic management, Goals represent the broad, concrete developmental steps and strategic milestones an organization establishes to translate its vision and mission into operational reality. On the exam paper, option C is marked.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C (Goal). Goals define the overarching major steps; objectives provide SMART operational targets.

cards.front: The RENI is intended to meet the nutrient needs of ________ people.
cards.rationale: Recommended Energy and Nutrient Intakes (RENI / PDRI) are explicitly formulated to meet the physiological requirements of practically all (97.5%) healthy individuals in a given population group. They do not apply to individuals suffering from acute illness, severe malnutrition, or therapeutic metabolic disorders.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. RENI applies strictly to healthy populations, not diseased or therapeutic clinical states.

cards.front: What is the measure of detecting early changes in body metabolism & nutrition before the appearance of overt clinical signs?
cards.rationale: Biochemical assessment (measuring serum micronutrients, enzyme activities, or urinary metabolites) detects early subclinical alterations in nutritional status and metabolic pathways prior to clinical manifestations.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Verbatim repeat of Item 53.

cards.front: The average weight gain during the first trimester of pregnancy is ________ kgs.
cards.rationale: According to the Institute of Medicine (IOM) and Philippine clinical nutrition guidelines, the expected maternal weight gain for a woman with normal pre-pregnancy BMI during the entire first trimester is approximately 1.0 to 2.0 or 2.3 kg (2.2 to 5.0 lbs).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. First trimester weight gain is minimal (1 to 2.3 kg); rapid gain occurs in 2nd and 3rd trimesters (~0.4 kg/week).

cards.front: The amino acid essential to infants is ________
cards.rationale: Histidine is well established in nutritional biochemistry as conditionally indispensable (essential) for infants due to immature endogenous biosynthetic pathways. Dietary histidine is required to maintain positive nitrogen balance and normal linear growth in infancy.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper: Note that Item 152 repeats this exact question stem, where option D was circled on the candidate's test paper. Histidine is the classic 9th essential amino acid in infants.

cards.front: The detailed operational plans, including budgets, and goals and targets that are specific, measurable, attainable, relevant and time-bound is ________
cards.rationale: In program management terminology, a Project is an operational undertaking characterized by defined SMART goals, specific deliverables, assigned budget, and a fixed operational timeframe. On the exam paper, option B is marked.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B (project). Notice action plan and project share operational definitions; candidate marked B.

cards.front: The Sustainable Development Goals contains ________ goals and targets.
cards.rationale: The UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development consists of 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), underpinned by 169 targets.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Reiteration of Item 123 verifying knowledge of the 17 SDGs.

cards.front: The basic principle in planning that refers to the active participation of everybody in the decision making process is ________
cards.rationale: The principle of Involvement (or participatory planning) asserts that all stakeholders, community representatives, and program implementers must actively participate in identifying priorities and formulating decisions to ensure local ownership and sustainability.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Planning principles: Involvement = participatory decision-making; Comprehensiveness = covering all necessary elements; Workability = feasibility.

cards.front: What is the global reference diet for adults that is symbolically represented by half a plate of fruits, vegetables and nuts and the other half consists of primarily whole grains, plant proteins, unsaturated plant oils, modest amounts of meat and dairy, and some added sugars and starchy vegetables?
cards.rationale: The EAT-Lancet Commission on Food, Planet, Health (2019) introduced the 'Planetary Health Diet'. It establishes a global reference diet designed to nurture human health and stay within environmental planetary boundaries, characterized by a plate where half is fruits, vegetables, and nuts, and half is whole grains, plant-source proteins, and unsaturated oils.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. The EAT-Lancet Commission 2019 Planetary Diet balances human nutritional adequacy with planetary boundaries.

cards.front: This pertains to a public health nutritionist who has communication skills, ranging from writing professional reports to the development of health and nutrition information based on scientific evidences.
cards.rationale: The Public Health Nutrition Administrator leads communication systems, translating scientific evidence into health promotion materials, technical program reports, and multi-sector policy briefs.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Echoes Item 59 regarding administrative and communication competencies of the Public Health Nutritionist.

cards.front: What activity could be done to help the program planners understand their allies, neutral parties, and opponents in order to decide the most feasible route to accomplish their goals?
cards.rationale: Stakeholder Analysis (option A, 'Stakeholder') is the strategic planning tool used to systematically identify individuals and groups, analyze their interests, influence, and stance (allies, neutral parties, or opponents), and formulate effective advocacy and coalition strategies.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Stakeholder analysis categorizes allies, neutrals, and opponents to tailor advocacy pathways.

cards.front: Vitamin ________ is required for growth, epithelial integrity and immunity and essential for the maintenance of visual purple for vision in dim light.
cards.rationale: Vitamin A (11-cis-retinal) conjugates with the protein opsin in retinal rod cells to form Rhodopsin ('visual purple'), the photoreceptor pigment essential for scotopic (dim light) vision. Vitamin A (retinoic acid) also maintains epithelial tissue integrity and cellular immune defense.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Rhodopsin (visual purple) = 11-cis retinal + opsin in rods, mediating dim-light adaptation.

cards.front: Which of the following contains tabulated data on quantities of different nutrients and energy value per 100g per food item?
cards.rationale: The Philippine Food Composition Tables (FCT), developed and maintained by the Food and Nutrition Research Institute (FNRI-DOST), provide standardized analytical data on macro- and micronutrient quantities and caloric density per 100 grams edible portion of Philippine foods.
