cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. FCT provides proximate, mineral, and vitamin values per 100 g edible portion.

cards.front: What is the Act on Salt Iodization Nationwide popularly known as ASIN Law?
cards.rationale: Republic Act No. 8172, enacted on December 20, 1995, is an 'Act for Salt Iodization Nationwide' (ASIN Law). It mandates the iodization of all salt for human and animal consumption to eliminate Iodine Deficiency Disorders (IDD) in the Philippines.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. RA 8172 = ASIN Law (1995); RA 7600 = Rooming-In/Breastfeeding (1992); RA 7883 = Barangay Health Workers Benefits (1995).

cards.front: Which of the following nutrients supplies oxygen from the lungs to the different parts of the body?
cards.rationale: Iron is the central metal cofactor of the heme moiety within Hemoglobin, the erythrocyte metalloprotein that coordinates molecular oxygen in the pulmonary alveoli and transports it via systemic circulation to peripheral tissues.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Iron in hemoglobin binds oxygen for systemic tissue transport.

cards.front: How many programs does the Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition 2017 to 2022 compose of?
cards.rationale: The Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition (PPAN 2017–2022) comprises exactly 12 strategic programs: 8 Nutrition-Specific programs, 1 Nutrition-Sensitive program cluster, and 3 Enabling support programs (subdivided into 46 specific projects).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Margin handwritten note next to A: '46 Projects'. PPAN structure: 12 Programs and 46 Projects.

cards.front: The world's time-bound and quantified targets for addressing extreme poverty in its many dimensions while promoting gender equality, education, environmental sustainability and basic human rights by 2030 is the ________
options: D. Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition
cards.rationale: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), spearheaded by the United Nations, represent the 15-year global commitment (2015–2030) targeting poverty eradication, reduced inequalities, quality education, universal healthcare, and environmental sustainability.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. 2030 global horizon = Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). MDGs covered 2000-2015.

cards.front: Translating the PPAN into a dynamic action plan and program at the grassroot level is called ________
cards.back: Barangay Plan of Action for Nutrition
options: A. Barangay Plan of Action for Nutrition
cards.rationale: In the Philippine decentralized local governance framework, the Barangay Nutrition Committee (BNC) translates national PPAN priorities into local operational reality via the Barangay Nutrition Action Plan (BNAP / BPAN).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Grassroots (barangay) level translation of PPAN = Barangay Nutrition Action Plan (BNAP/BPAN).

cards.front: What is the process of sharing information using different channels?
cards.rationale: Communication is the interactive process of generating, transmitting, receiving, and interpreting messages, information, and ideas through various interpersonal, print, electronic, and digital channels.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Basic definition of communication in health promotion and social marketing.

cards.front: The interpretation of data to determine whether a person or groups of people are well nourished or malnourished is called ________
cards.rationale: Nutritional Assessment is the systematic process of collecting, interpreting, and integrating anthropometric, biochemical, clinical, and dietary information to determine whether individuals or populations are adequately nourished or malnourished.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Interpretation of nutritional status data = Nutritional Assessment.

cards.front: Among underfive children, 25% are stunted. What is the severity of stunting using the WHO cut-off?
cards.rationale: Under the WHO/UNICEF (2018) revised thresholds for public health significance of stunting among children under 5 years: Very Low = < 2.5%; Low = 2.5 to < 10%; Medium = 10 to < 20%; High = 20 to < 30%; Very High = >= 30%. A prevalence of 25% falls directly into the 'High' severity category.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B (High). Under WHO stunting thresholds, 20% to <30% is High; >=30% is Very High.

cards.front: The type of research that employs systematic reviews of several research results and conduct statistical analysis to arrive at a conclusion is
cards.rationale: A Meta-Analysis is a high-level quantitative epidemiological study design that pools and statistically integrates the results from multiple independent primary studies identified through a systematic review to generate a single pooled effect size.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Margin handwritten note: 'merging ng findings ng ibang research and may statistical analysis'. Meta-analysis = statistical synthesis of multiple studies.

cards.front: The program and activities of DOH that aims to reduce childhood illnesses and eliminates micronutrient malnutrition.
cards.rationale: Garantisadong Pambata (GP) is the institutionalized DOH national child health campaign conducted semiannually to deliver a comprehensive integrated package: Vitamin A capsules, deworming tablets, routine immunizations, iron drops, and infant feeding promotion to under-five children.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Garantisadong Pambata delivers the biannual integrated package (Vit A + deworming + immunization).

cards.front: The 24-hour urinary nitrogen is a recovery biomarker for calcium. This statement is ________
cards.rationale: This statement is FALSE. 24-hour urinary nitrogen (UUN) is the gold-standard recovery biomarker for dietary PROTEIN intake (since ~80–90% of nitrogen from catabolized dietary protein is excreted in urine as urea), not calcium.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A (false). 24-hour urinary nitrogen is the recovery biomarker for dietary protein intake.

cards.front: The amino acid essential to infants is ________
cards.rationale: On this examination paper, option D ('tryptophan') is circled. In classical biochemistry, histidine (Option A) is widely recognized as the conditionally essential amino acid specific to infants due to rate-limiting biosynthetic capacity. Note candidate circled D here, while Item 132 featured the same question.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D (tryptophan). Candidate marked D on paper; biochemically, Histidine is the conditionally indispensable amino acid for infant growth.

cards.front: A strategy to encourage food manufacturers to fortify their products with one or more nutrients is called the ________
cards.rationale: The Sangkap Pinoy Seal Program (SPSP) is a voluntary fortification advocacy initiative developed by the Department of Health (DOH) under RA 8976, granting a recognizable seal of quality to processed food products fortified with essential micronutrients (Vitamin A, Iron, or Iodine).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Sangkap Pinoy Seal Program = voluntary fortification seal for processed foods.

cards.front: This pertains to planned actions that are implemented to improve nutrition and well-being of designated groups.
cards.rationale: Nutrition Interventions are purposefully planned and targeted actions designed to positively modify nutritional intake, eating behavior, physiological status, or environmental determinants in specific high-risk groups.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Echoes Item 10 defining nutrition interventions.

cards.front: What is the collegial body of NNC that is chaired by the Secretary of Health with other member agencies?
cards.rationale: The NNC Governing Board is the apex collegial and multi-sectoral policy-making body for nutrition in the country, chaired by the Secretary of Health and composed of heads of 10 executive departments and 3 private sector representatives.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Highest nutrition policy body in the Philippines is the NNC Governing Board.

cards.front: During infancy the brain reaches ________ % of its adult size at 12 to 24 months.
cards.rationale: During the first two years of life (the First 1,000 Days), brain development accelerates dramatically: reaching ~50% of adult brain weight by 6 months, ~60–70% by 12 months, and approximately 75% to 80% by 24 months of age, underpinning the urgency of early nutritional protection against stunting.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Brain reaches ~75% of adult volume/weight by age 2 (24 months).

cards.front: The President can use this document to set policy while avoiding public debate and opposition and it does not require congressional approval.
cards.rationale: Historically during the martial law era (1972–1986), the Philippine President issued Presidential Decrees (PDs) having the full force of national law without congressional debate or approval (e.g. PD 491 creating the NNC). In constitutional republics, Executive Orders direct executive operations without congress. On this exam paper, option A is marked.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A (Presidential Decree). Historically, PDs bypassed congress (e.g., PD 491, PD 1569). Executive Orders (C/D) also direct policy without legislative passage.

cards.front: The method/s to assess moderate or severe malnutrition among children is/are ________
cards.rationale: Comprehensive screening and diagnostic evaluation of acute malnutrition in community and clinical settings integrates Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC < 115 mm for SAM, 115–<125 mm for MAM), assessment of bilateral pitting edema, and head/growth parameters. On the exam paper, option A (all of these) is marked.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. MUAC, bilateral pitting edema, and anthropometric indices collectively identify SAM and MAM.

cards.front: What is the award given to a municipality, city, or province that has shown outstanding performance in implementing its local nutrition action plan in the region?
cards.rationale: The Green Banner Award (now Green Banner Seal of Compliance under MELLPI Pro) is conferred annually by Regional Nutrition Evaluation Teams (RNET) and the NNC to LGUs (municipality, city, province) that achieve exemplary performance in nutrition program implementation and significant malnutrition reductions.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Green Banner Award = highest regional recognition for exemplary LGU nutrition program performance. MELLPI is the evaluation tool.

cards.front: What is the term given to a collection of organizational resources that is geared to accomplish a certain major goal and have limited duration and a defined set of deliverables?
cards.rationale: In project management terminology, a Project is defined as a temporary endeavor with a defined beginning and end, undertaken to meet specific goals with designated deliverables. On the candidate's exam paper, option C ('Plan') is marked. Both concepts are central to public health administration.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C (Plan). In classical PMBOK definition, a temporary endeavor with limited duration and defined deliverables is a Project (B); candidate marked C.

cards.front: The science and art of applying the principles of nutrition to the planning and preparation of foods, and management of the diet in relation to both health and disease.
cards.rationale: Verbatim duplicate of Item 9. On this question, the candidate marked option D ('meal planning and mangement'), while on Item 9 option A ('dietetics') was marked.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Identical question stem to Item 9 (where A was marked). Highlights the dual emphasis on Dietetics as a discipline and Meal Planning & Management as an applied art.

cards.front: The nutrient that prevents hemorrhagic disease during pregnancy is vitamin ________
cards.rationale: Vitamin K is an obligate cofactor for hepatic gamma-glutamyl carboxylase, which carboxylates glutamic acid residues on prothrombin (Factor II) and clotting factors VII, IX, and X. Maternal vitamin K adequacy and newborn intramuscular prophylactic Vitamin K1 (phytomenadione) prevent Hemorrhagic Disease of the Newborn (Vitamin K Deficiency Bleeding / VKDB).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Vitamin K prevents hemorrhagic disease of the newborn (VKDB) via clotting factor activation.

cards.front: The process of collecting information to determine whether activities are implemented as planned is ________
cards.rationale: Monitoring is the routine, continuous tracking of project activities, inputs, and outputs to assess whether activities are being carried out according to the planned schedule, budget, and operational protocols.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Monitoring tracks ongoing implementation against plans; Evaluation measures ultimate results and impact.

cards.front: A combination of two anthropometric measurements is called ________
cards.rationale: In anthropometric methodology, an Index is formed by combining two raw measurements (such as weight and height to create weight-for-height) or a measurement with a biological variable (such as height and age to form height-for-age).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Measurement + Measurement = Index; Index + Cut-off = Indicator. See Item 71.

cards.front: The long range direction that answers the question of what you must focus on to achieve the vision is ________
cards.rationale: A Mission statement clearly articulates the fundamental focus, core activities, and operational purpose of an organization or program to fulfill its long-term Vision.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Verbatim repeat of Item 47.

cards.front:
Situation 1 - Nutrition education and other nutrition interventions are implemented in a community-based approach with core programs and services that involve and engage the community - wide participation. The development and utilization of a documented plan will assist the Nutritionist - Dietitian in developing goals, message, and methods in an effective and cohesive way, resulting in better use of resources and more targeted outcomes.

What is your first step in developing your program plan?
options: C. Know and identify the problem
cards.rationale: Situation 1 Question 1: Problem identification / situational assessment is invariably the prerequisite first phase of the program planning cycle. Planners must assess local needs, epidemiologic burden, and root causes before setting targets or formulating strategies.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Reiteration of Item 8 and Item 32 under Situation 1.

cards.front: Situation 1 - In gathering data, you need to collect qualitative data. What are the commonly used methods for gathering qualitative data?
cards.back: Conduct of key informant interviews, focus groups, and participant observation
options: D. Conduct of key informant interviews, focus groups, and participant observation
cards.rationale: Situation 1 Question 2: Qualitative data collection methodologies in community nutrition research comprise participatory techniques: Key Informant Interviews (KIIs), Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), direct participant observation, and semi-structured community dialogues.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Qualitative methods capture beliefs, cultural norms, and contextual nuances through KIIs, FGDs, and observation.

cards.front: Situation 1 - What are the most common methods for collecting quantitative data?
options: A. Surveys and questionnaires revealing measurements in numbers or prevalences
cards.rationale: Situation 1 Question 3: In epidemiological research, surveys with structured questionnaires and standardized measurements yield numerical, prevalence, and incidence data. On the candidate's examination paper, option B ('Getting biochemical markers') is marked as a quantitative laboratory method.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Note: Option A represents standard community quantitative surveys; examinee marked B.

cards.front: Situation 1 - What is type of data that offers descriptive information that may capture experience, behavior, opinion, value, feeling, knowledge, sensory response, or observable phenomena?
cards.rationale: Situation 1 Question 4: Qualitative data provides rich descriptive, narrative, and contextual insight into human behavior, cultural beliefs, values, emotions, and motivations that cannot be reduced to simple numerical scores.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Qualitative data = non-numerical descriptive information exploring experiences and beliefs.

cards.front: Situation 1 - What is the step in your project planning where you answer the bottom-line question: Are we getting better, getting worse, or staying the same?
cards.rationale: Situation 1 Question 5: Situational Analysis evaluates past and present trends to determine community nutritional trajectory—answering whether the population's nutritional status is improving, deteriorating, or remaining stagnant compared to historical baselines.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D (top of page 17). Situational analysis establishes current status and directional trajectory.

cards.front:
Situation 2 - For the first time, a child was seen as having diarrhea and with weight - for- age z score of 2 SD. His height was also < 2SD. After 3 months he was again brought for consultation and you noticed that he was underweight.

Considering the weight of the child, he is diagnosed as ________
cards.rationale: Situation 2 Question 1: On the child's initial visit, his weight-for-age Z-score was reported at 2 SD (or within the -2 to +2 SD band). Under WHO Child Growth Standards, a Z-score between -2 SD and +2 SD is classified as Normal weight-for-age.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D (normal). At visit 1, WFA Z-score within +-2 SD denotes normal weight.

cards.front: Situation 2 - What is the indicator of nutritional status of the child on his second visit at 3 months?
cards.rationale: Situation 2 Question 2: The case vignette explicitly specifies: 'After 3 months he was again brought for consultation and you noticed that he was underweight.' Thus, the diagnosed indicator on the second visit is Underweight.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C (underweight). Following prolonged diarrhea and illness, the child progressed to underweight.

cards.front: Situation 2 - Considering the height of the child, he is considered as ________
cards.rationale: Situation 2 Question 3: The vignette states that the child's height was '< 2SD' (meaning height-for-age Z-score < -2 SD). By definition, height-for-age < -2 SD is classified as Stunted (chronic linear growth restriction).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Height-for-age < -2 SD indicates stunting.

cards.front: Situation 2 - What supplement would best be given to the child on his first visit?
cards.rationale: Situation 2 Question 4: Under the Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI) and DOH/WHO protocols for acute diarrhea, Oral Zinc supplementation (20 mg elemental zinc daily for 10–14 days, or 10 mg for infants < 6 months) accelerates mucosal regeneration and reduces episode severity. High-dose Vitamin A is administered if due or in cases of persistent diarrhea/deficiency.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Zinc (10-20 mg/day x 10-14 days) and Vitamin A are standard adjuncts in pediatric diarrhea management.

cards.front: Situation 2 - Underweight is considered as ________ of nutritional status.
cards.rationale: Situation 2 Question 5: In nutritional epidemiology, underweight is broadly an indicator of nutritional status; on the candidate's examination paper, option C ('threshold') is marked, highlighting the statistical cut-off/threshold (-2 SD) that defines the classification.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C (threshold). Note: In standard terminology, underweight is an indicator established by a statistical threshold (<-2 SD); examinee circled C.

cards.front:
Situation 3 - A Nutritionist-Dietitian was employed at the evacuation center, she observed that children are suffering from SAM and have severe diarrhea. The prevalence of underweight is 20 %, stunting, 29%, but overweight among adults is 20%. Many of the infants aged 8 to 11 months are not breastfed because mothers claim that they do not have breastmilk. Many pregnant women are pale, weak and cannot work for an extended time due to fatigue.

What do you do with the children who are suffering from SAM with severe diarrhea?
cards.back: Refer to hospital for in-patient care and management
options: A. Call the Nurse or Physician in the RHU
B. Refer to hospital for in-patient care and management
C. Do counselling, feed the child and observe the effects
D. Refer to hospital for out-patient care
cards.rationale: Situation 3 Question 1: Under the Philippine National Guidelines on the Management of Severe Acute Malnutrition (PIMAM), children with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) complicated by medical conditions such as severe diarrhea, dehydration, persistent vomiting, or systemic infection MUST be immediately referred for In-patient Therapeutic Care (stabilization with F-75 formula and medical resuscitation).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Complicated SAM (SAM + severe diarrhea/dehydration) mandates inpatient hospitalization.

cards.front: Situation 3 - What does the 20% prevalence of underweight among children indicates in terms of its magnitude and severity as a public health problem?
cards.rationale: Situation 3 Question 2: WHO population-level classification of public health severity for underweight among children under 5: Low: < 10%; Medium: 10% to 19%; High: 20% to 29%; Very High: >= 30%. At exactly 20%, underweight prevalence is classified as 'High'.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C (High). WHO underweight severity: 20-29% is High.

cards.front: Situation 3 - What does the 29% prevalence of stunting among children indicates in terms of its magnitude and severity as a public health problem?
cards.rationale: Situation 3 Question 3: Under WHO criteria, stunting prevalence between 20% and 29% is classified as 'High' public health significance (>= 30% is Very High; under the 2018 WHO/UNICEF thresholds, 20 to <30% is High). Thus, 29% indicates High severity.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C (High). WHO stunting severity: 20-29% = High; >=30% = Very High.

cards.front: Situation 3 - What do you advise to mothers with infants who discontinued breastfeeding?
cards.back: Continue breastfeeding while giving appropriate complementary foods
options: B. Continue breastfeeding while giving appropriate complementary foods
C. Give infants carbohydrates rich foods to increase energy
D. Give foods to infants from the common pot
cards.rationale: Situation 3 Question 4: For infants 8–11 months in emergencies, health workers must support mothers to relactate and continue frequent breastfeeding while introducing nutrient-dense, hygienic complementary foods, protecting against waterborne infection and death in evacuation centers.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled B. Counsel on relactation and continued breastfeeding up to 2 years alongside complementary foods.

cards.front: The paleness, weakness and easy fatigability among women are clinical signs of ________
cards.rationale: Pallor (paleness of conjunctivae, palms, and mucosal membranes), chronic fatigue, and general weakness are hallmark clinical manifestations of anemia (reduced circulating hemoglobin and systemic tissue hypoxia).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Clinical triad of anemia: paleness, fatigue, and muscular weakness.

cards.front:
Situation 4 - Manar is 39 years old, pregnant in her 5th month and has a 10 month old female infant. She went to the health facility for her 1st pre-natal check - up and was endorsed to you by the Registered Nurse for nutrition services.

As RND what do you need to do first?
options: C. Counsel her on right foods
cards.rationale: Situation 4 Question 1: In the Nutrition Care Process (NCP) and clinical triage, the RND conducts a dietary assessment / 24-hour food intake recall (dietary interview) to determine actual nutrient intake, eating patterns, and nutritional risks before counseling or prescribing interventions. On the exam paper, option D is marked.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Assessment precedes intervention: interview on food intake before providing counseling or supplements.

cards.front: Situation 4 - What would be your advice?
cards.back: Advise her to take more foods using household measures referring to pinggang pinoy
options: B. Advice the weight of foods to be taken using pinggang pinoy
C. Advise her to take more foods using household measures referring to pinggang pinoy
cards.rationale: Situation 4 Question 2: In community nutrition education, pregnant women are guided using practical, familiar household measures (cups, tablespoons, fist sizes) integrated with the visual proportions of Pinggang Pinoy for Pregnant and Lactating Women, ensuring practical compliance.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Use household measures referring to Pinggang Pinoy for accessible community nutrition counseling.

cards.front: Situation 4 - How much additional caloric intake would she achieve?
cards.rationale: Situation 4 Question 3: Manar is in her 5th month of gestation (2nd trimester). According to the Philippine Dietary Reference Intakes (PDRI 2015), the recommended additional daily energy intake during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy is +300 kcal/day.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled C. Margin handwritten note: 'pag 3trim +300 +150'. PDRI 2nd & 3rd trimester pregnancy energy allowance = +300 kcal/day.

cards.front: Situation 4 - In consideration with her 10 month old child what would you advice since she is no longer breastfeeding?
options: A. Subject the child for new born screening
B. Maintain the weight of her infant
C. Feed the child with more caloric foods to gain weight
cards.rationale: Situation 4 Question 4: For a 10-month-old older infant who is not breastfed, optimal growth requires providing nutrient-dense, hygienic, varied complementary foods (including animal-source foods, legumes, vegetables, and energy-dense staples) along with adequate clean milk feeds.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Provide nutritious complementary foods suited to older infancy (9-11 months).

cards.front: Situation 4 - What would be the recommended energy would she achieve for her 10 month old infant?
cards.rationale: Situation 4 Question 5: Under the Philippine Dietary Reference Intakes (PDRI), the estimated daily energy requirement for an infant aged 9 to 11 months is approximately 630–700 kcal/day (or ~80 kcal/kg/day). Option A (630 kcal) is the target value.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. PDRI energy requirement for 9-11 months infant = ~630 kcal/day.

cards.front:
Situation 5 - A woman aged 60 years went for check-up at the health center because she was weak. She was found to be suffering from chronic energy deficiency, anemia, endemic goiter and has xerophtalmia.

What is her BMI"?
cards.rationale: Situation 5 Question 1: Chronic Energy Deficiency (CED) in adults is defined by the WHO and FNRI as a Body Mass Index (BMI) of less than 18.5 kg/m2 (Grade I CED: 17.0–18.4; Grade II: 16.0–16.9; Grade III: < 16.0 kg/m2).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Adult CED = BMI < 18.5 kg/m2.

cards.front: Situation 5 - What is her haemoglobin level in g/L?
cards.rationale: Situation 5 Question 2: According to the World Health Organization (WHO) diagnostic thresholds, anemia in non-pregnant adult women (aged 15+ years) is defined by a blood hemoglobin concentration of less than 120 g/L (or < 12.0 g/dL).
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. WHO cutoff: Anemia in non-pregnant women = Hb < 120 g/L (< 12 g/dL); Men = < 130 g/L; Pregnant women = < 110 g/L.

cards.front: Situation 5 - Goiter is a deficiency of ________
cards.rationale: Situation 5 Question 3: Endemic goiter (hyperplasia and hypertrophy of the thyroid gland) is the classic clinical manifestation of chronic Iodine Deficiency Disorders (IDD), caused by compensatory TSH overstimulation in response to insufficient thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3) production.
cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled D. Goiter results from chronic iodine deficiency (IDD). Addressed by RA 8172 (ASIN Law).

cards.userNotes: Exam paper circled A. Xerophthalmia = Vitamin A deficiency eye signs.
